function.name: Media_3_FindMovies
function.description: Search for movies that fit a user's preferences such as genre and starring actors. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

genre.description: The genre of the movie to search for.

starring.description: The name of a specific actor or actress the user wants to see in the movie. Use 'All' to include any.

function.name: Media_3_PlayMovie
function.description: Streams a selected movie online with the option to choose subtitles in various languages. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

title.description: The title of the movie to be streamed.

subtitle_language.description: The preferred language for the movie's subtitles.

function.name: Music_3_PlayMedia
function.description: Plays a specified track on a designated media player device. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

track.description: The title of the song to be played.

artist.description: The name of the artist performing the song. If unspecified, any artist is acceptable.

device.description: The media player device where the song will be played.

album.description: The album where the song is featured. If unspecified, any album is acceptable.

function.name: Music_3_LookupMusic
function.description: Retrieve a list of songs that align with the user's musical preferences based on artist, album, genre, and release year. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

artist.description: The name of the artist or band. Use 'dontcare' if this is not a filtering criterion.

album.description: The title of the album. Use 'dontcare' if this is not a filtering criterion.

genre.description: The musical genre of the songs. Select 'dontcare' to include all genres.

year.description: The release year of the song. Use 'dontcare' to include songs from any year.

message.reasoning:
The user says: "Could you assist me to find some songs? I love Popular songs, song by Kesha and I have been told an album called Rainbow is fab"

We need to interpret the request. They want to find some songs. They mention they love popular songs, songs by Kesha, and an album called Rainbow is fab. So we should ask clarifying questions about what exactly they want. Possibly they want to find songs that match those criteria. We can use the Music_3_LookupMusic function. But we need to confirm what they want: do they want to find songs by Kesha from the album Rainbow? Or do they want to find popular songs from the album Rainbow? Or do they want to find songs that are popular and by Kesha? The user says "I love Popular songs, song by Kesha and I have been told an album called Rainbow is fab". That could mean they want to find songs that are popular, by Kesha, and from the album Rainbow. Or maybe they want to find songs that are popular, songs by Kesha, and songs from the album Rainbow. It's ambiguous.

We should ask clarifying question: "Do you want to find songs that are popular, by Kesha, and from the album Rainbow?" Or "Would you like to find songs that are popular, songs by Kesha, and songs from the album Rainbow separately?" We can ask them to clarify. Then we can proceed accordingly.

We also might want to ask if they'd like to play any of them. But first we need to clarify.
